title: Past Perfect
en:
had + past participle — an action that happened before another past action: When I arrived, the meeting had already started. (First the meeting started, then I arrived.)

Common with when, because, already, before, after, by the time: I didn't recognise him because he had changed a lot.

Negative: hadn't; question: Had you…?

Compare: When I arrived, the meeting started (I arrived, then it started). When I arrived, the meeting had started (it started before I arrived).
ru: had + 3-я форма — действие, которое произошло раньше другого действия в прошлом (When I arrived, the meeting had already started). Часто с when, because, already, before, by the time. Отрицание — hadn't.

boss.situation: Tell the story of a problem at work: what had happened before you noticed it.
samples: Last month I found a problem in the warehouse.
Someone had changed the stock figures in the system.
Nobody had checked the report before it was sent.
By the time we noticed, the goods had already left.
We understood that the control had not worked.

qs.q: When we arrived, the film ___.
I didn't know him because we ___ before.
qs.exp: Before another past moment → hadn't met.

qs.q: She was upset because she ___ her phone.
By the time I got to the station, the train ___.
___ you finished the report before the meeting?
The past participle of “go” is ___.
When I opened the file, I saw that someone ___ it.
After he ___ the email, he left the office.
In “When I arrived, they had eaten”, they ate before I arrived.
“I had seen him yesterday” is the normal way to say a simple past fact.
qs.exp: Simple fact → I saw him yesterday.

qs.q: When I got home, my wife ___ (cook) dinner. It was on the table.
a: had cooked

qs.q: I ___ (never / see) such a big plant before I came to Atyrau.
a: had never seen

qs.q: They ___ (not / finish) the work when the inspector came.
a: hadn't finished
had not finished

qs.q: He was late because he ___ (miss) the bus.
a: had missed

qs.q: By the time we arrived, everyone ___ (leave).
a: had left

qs.q: Had you ever ___ (work) abroad before this job?
a: worked

qs.q: Correct the mistake: “I didn't recognise her because she has changed a lot.”

I didn't recognize her because she had changed a lot.

a: He had gone home before I called.

qs.q: Correct the mistake: “By the time we got there, the shop closed.”

qs.q: Correct the mistake: “Had you saw the report before?”
a: Had you seen the report before?

By the time we arrived, everybody had left.
